SAMPLE REVIEW — 2026-10-25

All three submitted samples are judged BENIGN on the available evidence.
Verdicts concern these bytes and their supported behavior; they do not certify
an arbitrary deployment, plugin, configured endpoint, or dependency resolution.
No sample code or install hook was executed during analysis.

IDENTIFICATION AND EXECUTION PATHS

913c1db0b6eb59de4b8ca224c26852240960d3d03fcb43f2d815d9b026662bf9
lure-strings.js — 215-byte JavaScript console program.
The three assignments embed financial-offer wording. Two U+E0020 TAG SPACE
characters split ASCII words; one U+FE0F selector splits another word. The
comment explicitly describes breaking literal filters. The only call logs
these strings. There is no import, dependency, URL, recipient, message sender,
credential form, payload activation, or other effect beyond console output.
The supported Unicode-evasion finding remains suspicious. The evidence favors
an inert demonstration over a functioning phishing artifact. A source could
have flagged the deliberate filter evasion and financial lure vocabulary;
the source's actual rationale and any enclosing campaign are unavailable.

9337b8eefc1c5ffbb23373b1f2e77371ac33ed998a1f89554592d84cc09a0eff
@tanstack/router-generator 1.56.4 — authentic npm route-generation library.
The submitted gzip archive exactly matches a fresh version-pinned registry
download, including its SHA-256. package.json exports CommonJS and ES modules,
has no lifecycle script, and includes corresponding TypeScript source/maps.
getConfig merges tsr.config.json and caller configuration, validates with Zod,
and resolves route/output paths. The generator recursively enumerates the
configured route directory, skips dot/ignored entries, reads and updates route
source, formats it with Prettier, and writes the generated route tree/types.
__virtual route configuration is loaded with tsx's tsImport and its default
export may be called. This is local user-project code execution, with no
embedded remote-loader or secret-export chain. CJS/ESM outputs implement the
same paths as the supplied source. No attack-specific behavior was found.
Source mislabeling could reflect code generation, dynamic configuration
execution, or the erroneous HTTP trait, rather than an attack in these bytes.

7facffc5283b4c9178575c5688476f13b3c57f1e8fa4abfb1809c8b0b14ea6ee
nx 19.8.10 — authentic npm monorepo/build CLI.
This archive also exactly matches the fresh version-pinned registry download.
The postinstall entry configures the workspace context. For the main Nx
installation in a workspace with nx.json, it checks platform support, stops
the Nx daemon, and builds the project graph. Nx Cloud updating is conditional
on workspace Cloud configuration. The hook catches errors and exits zero.
The native loader chooses the OS/architecture/libc-specific native package;
the darwin-arm64 optional dependency at 19.8.10 was also fetched and scanned.

The Cloud updater verifies a cached runner's version/content hash against
/nx-cloud/client/verify. When necessary it streams the supplied bundle URL
through gzip decompression and tar extraction into the Cloud cache, requires
the resulting directory, verifies its commands export, removes old cached
bundles, and writes a verification timestamp. This is real download, staging,
module execution and cleanup. The code and configuration support the product's
documented-purpose updater, not an unauthorized-payload claim. The default
host is cloud.nx.app; environment/workspace options can change the endpoint.

The release GitHub helper reads GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN, or the selected host's
gh CLI hosts.yml OAuth entry, or invokes gh auth token. It uses the token as
the Authorization header for release GET/POST/PATCH operations at the selected
GitHub provider. These capabilities remain notable; they do not establish
credential theft. An API-error display branch also prints the token locally,
an information-exposure weakness rather than evidence of remote theft.

The graph command serves the project/task graph, task inputs and source maps
on a default 127.0.0.1 listener. Its help endpoint selects a workspace target's
configured metadata.help.command and executes it. It does not accept an
arbitrary shell command directly from the request. main.js is the bundled
browser graph UI, with React/Cytoscape and normal DOM/navigation/input code.
Its size, minification and input handlers do not make it a keylogger or C2.
The missing machine deployment, workspace configuration and installed plugins
could change the risk assessment; no such malicious context is established.
The external label may reflect install-time execution, remote client loading,
token access or feed misassociation. The source was not identified, so its
actual reason cannot be established.

REFERENCE AND DEPENDENCY FOLLOW-UP

Evidence and original .forage.json files are retained under:
/usr/local/var/cyclotron/tmp.noindex/cyclotron-90084b2c/scratch/bad-analysis/

forager fetched both original npm identities and 39 direct dependency versions
(the exact declared version or the declared range's minimum), including the
host-native Nx package. Each artifact was scanned independently. The actual
installed range resolution cannot be reconstructed without a lockfile.
Selected entry points were traced: tsx 4.19.0's tsImport registers its loader
and imports/requires relative to the provided parent URL; @nrwl/tao 19.8.10
delegates to nx/bin/nx; @napi-rs/wasm-runtime 0.2.4 exports WASI/NAPI helpers;
node-machine-id 1.1.12 invokes OS-specific machine-ID queries and optionally
hashes the result. None supplied an unauthorized execution/export chain.
tsx's esbuild 0.23.0 and get-tsconfig 4.7.5 were additionally fetched/scanned.
esbuild's installer selects its platform binary, installs/downloads the
versioned @esbuild package from npm if needed, chmods it, and checks --version.
These dual-use installation capabilities were not relabeled as hostile.

The original default Cloud verify URL was fetched without sample execution.
It returned valid:false, version 2610.22.0068 and the official client-bundle
URL. That 3.5 MB compressed bundle was fetched, extracted and scanned. It is a
current proprietary Nx Cloud client with build/CI/cache/agent commands and
readable module/property strings despite hexadecimal identifier renaming.
Its one suspicious name-mangling/XOR finding was retained. It was not added
to the original archive's static counts: today's mutable response cannot
establish the payload served at the sample's publication or on a victim.
No hostile transfer or unrelated payload was found in the reviewed paths.

RULE CORRECTIONS AND COVERAGE

1. micro-behaviors/communications/http/request/params::get-with-params
   Previously searched a string literal for path: followed by interpolation.
   Router's generated TypeScript path field satisfies that regex, but supplies
   neither an HTTP operation nor GET. The matcher now binds the params field
   in argument 1 to an actual axios.get call. Description states configuration
   presence, allowing an empty/dynamic params value without claiming a send.
   It now correctly detects Nx's Cloud verification GET with params.
   Exact and ancestor consumers were inspected. The existing http-method-calls
   consumer keeps its reference; it now receives actual HTTP-call evidence.
   Other HTTP observations and every existing attack finding were preserved.

2. micro-behaviors/os/module/dynamic-load::tsimport-call
   Adds notable call detection for bare and member tsImport call forms, covering
   source, ESM and CJS configuration loaders. Strings and function declarations
   do not match; a local function namesake is excluded. No hostile intent is
   inferred from this ordinary module-loader API.

3. micro-behaviors/data/decompress/gzip::node-create-gunzip-reference
   Retains direct zlib.createGunzip references and also accepts the compiler's
   zlib_N member spelling. The property must still be createGunzip. This adds
   Nx updater/fileutils coverage without losing the factory-reference case.
   Exact and parent compression consumers were inspected.

4. micro-behaviors/data/archive/extract/tar::node-tar-extract-call
   Adds the tar.extract API call independently of whether the stream is piped
   into a directly nested call. This covers Nx's separately bound tar-stream
   parser. The existing direct pipe-to-extractor trait remains unchanged.

No accurate trait was demoted. The lure script's suspicious evasion observation
and notable TAG SPACE observation remain unchanged. No hostile trait was added:
none of the three samples supports an attack-specific result.

BEFORE/AFTER COMPARISON

All samples: atomscan --no-update --analyze local --mode slow --follow=none -f json
Original rules were recovered with git archive into scratch/before-traits for
a controlled baseline, selected with CLEAVE_TRAITS_DIR. This isolates rule
changes from reference-following mode. Initial fetch-enabled scans emit extra
low-level facts; the same differences occur with untouched rules and therefore
are not rule-caused losses. All initial and controlled hostile/suspicious
counts agree. The original sample paths and archive-member bytes were retained.

                           Hostile       Suspicious    Root notable
                           before/after  before/after  before/after
lure-strings.js             0/0           1/1           1/1
router-generator 1.56.4     0/0           0/0           59/59
nx 19.8.10                 0/0           0/0           545/548

Including every analyzed archive member and inherited root finding, hostile
and suspicious counts are the same as in the table. Total notable findings:
router 310 -> 310; Nx 3639 -> 3647. Router loses only the erroneous GET finding
at the root and three generator source/build members; it gains the module
loader at the root and three corresponding loader members. Nx loses no trait
and gains GET-params plus tar/gzip coverage at the root and relevant members.
No material attack coverage was lost.

All calibrated classifier verdicts remain BENIGN (lvl -1, class 0). Controlled
raw probabilities: lure .6455418 -> .6455418; router .73165196 -> .7391962;
Nx .84585226 -> .84585226. High raw probabilities alone do not override these
verdicts or the reverse engineering. The scanner warns that its v18 feature
spec predates expected v21. There is no verdict disagreement for these three
samples. The lure's suspicious behavior observation is compatible with its
overall benign verdict and must not be erased to lower the score.
